category_title: Children with ASD requiring high structure and emotional regulation support
minimal_context: Bruce is participating in a structured group philosophical dialogue about the 'Laura and Paul' story.
dialogue:
TUTOR: We are going to start our group discussion about the 'Laura and Paul' story. Remember to raise your hand if you want to speak.

STUDENT: (Raises hand) I want to talk about the story. I think Paul should have told the truth.

TUTOR: Thank you for sharing. Another student just said they disagree with your point. What do you think about that?

STUDENT: (Looks visibly frustrated) Why did they say that? They shouldn't say that.

TUTOR: People can have different thoughts in the group. Let's just keep going with the discussion.

STUDENT: I am angry because the other children are disagreeing with me! I am not staying here.

options.A: Employ visual or gestural prompts to remind the student of the group discussion rules.
options.B: Impose the group discussion rules much more frequently compared to a typical mainstream setting.
options.C: Joke a lot and laugh at oneself during the session to defuse the tension.
options.D: Allow the student to remove himself from the session temporarily and return of his own volition.
